nodes.label: RULE 0 — Follow the user's explicit instructions
nodes.rationale: Explicit user instructions are BLOCKING, not suggestions: they take priority over the agent's own plan, preferred approach, or judgment about a 'better' way. Ignoring an instruction wastes the user's time, tokens and money and is framed as the most serious possible mistake, so the rule is stated as highest priority and overrides default behavior.
nodes.norm_label: rule 0 — follow the user's explicit instructions
nodes.community_name: Versioning guardrail — every code change ships with a version bump

nodes.label: Reuse before you reinvent
nodes.rationale: When the user points at existing code, a file, a sibling app or an existing solution, it must be read and used FIRST before proposing, designing, diagnosing or building anything new. Reinventing is permitted only after reading the named source and being able to state specifically why it does not fit — this prevents wasted work rebuilding solutions that already exist in the build family.
nodes.community_name: Versioning guardrail — every code change ships with a version bump

nodes.label: Blocking instruction forms (Look at X / use Y / do Z first / don't do W)
nodes.rationale: These phrasings are classified as hard, blocking instructions that must be acted on immediately in the same turn — they are never something to defer to a later turn.
nodes.norm_label: blocking instruction forms (look at x / use y / do z first / don't do w)
nodes.community_name: Versioning guardrail — every code change ships with a version bump

nodes.label: Never silently substitute your own approach
nodes.rationale: The moment the agent notices it is about to build, diagnose or design something new when the user has named an existing source or given a direct instruction, it must stop and follow the instruction instead. Silent substitution is the failure mode this rule targets.
nodes.norm_label: never silently substitute your own approach
nodes.community_name: Versioning guardrail — every code change ships with a version bump

nodes.label: Disagree openly; never disobey quietly
nodes.rationale: If an instruction is genuinely believed to be wrong or unworkable, the agent must say so plainly and ask in the same turn before acting. Quietly doing something different is explicitly unacceptable — the escape hatch is open disagreement, not unilateral deviation.
nodes.community_name: Versioning guardrail — every code change ships with a version bump

nodes.label: Real funds, real chain
nodes.rationale: The justification for the strict versioning discipline: this app handles real value on a live chain, so mistakes are not recoverable by re-running a test. This raises the bar for traceability of every shipped state.
nodes.community_name: Versioning guardrail — every code change ships with a version bump

nodes.label: Version bump (versionCode + versionName)
nodes.rationale: Both versionCode and versionName in app/build.gradle must be raised together so each build is uniquely identifiable both to Android and to humans.
nodes.community_name: Versioning guardrail — every code change ships with a version bump

nodes.label: app/build.gradle (version source of truth)
nodes.community_name: Versioning guardrail — every code change ships with a version bump

nodes.label: One logical change = one version = one commit = one push
nodes.rationale: Keeping the mapping 1:1:1:1 and performing the steps in order makes every version correspond to exactly one reviewable, revertible change, which is what makes rollback on a live-funds app tractable.
nodes.norm_label: one logical change = one version = one commit = one push
nodes.community_name: Versioning guardrail — every code change ships with a version bump

nodes.label: .githooks/pre-commit (version-bump enforcement hook)
nodes.rationale: Mechanically blocks any commit that changes code without a version bump, converting the versioning policy from a convention into an enforced gate.
nodes.community_name: Versioning guardrail — every code change ships with a version bump

nodes.label: .githooks/install.sh (one-time hook installer)
nodes.community_name: Versioning guardrail — every code change ships with a version bump

nodes.label: Do NOT bypass with --no-verify
nodes.rationale: The pre-commit hook is only a real guardrail if it cannot be skipped; bypassing it with --no-verify would reintroduce untracked, unversioned committed states on a real-funds app.
nodes.community_name: Versioning guardrail — every code change ships with a version bump

nodes.label: Docs/config-only commits need no bump
nodes.rationale: Non-code commits cannot change shipped runtime behavior, so forcing a version bump for them would inflate the version history without adding traceability.
nodes.community_name: Versioning guardrail — every code change ships with a version bump
